cards.subject: The First Sunday of Advent: on the stone step before a church altar, an evergreen Advent wreath of fir and holly with red berries and a few pine cones, holding four tall candles — three violet and one rose — only the first violet candle lit, its small flame steady. Behind it the altar, dressed in a violet frontal with a simple gold cross and gold orphreys, two brass candlesticks with plain white candles at its ends and only a little greenery, no flowers on the altar table. Above the altar, a round window shows a deep blue pre-dawn sky over a snowy village with a single bright morning star. No people. Quiet, expectant, nocturnal light. Keep everything inside the arched window.
cards.frame: a thin violet ruled line just inside the gold border; the inner window is ROUND-ARCHED like a church window, edged in gold and violet; no halo
cards.basis: The Advent wreath as the Directory on Popular Piety describes it (four candles lit Sunday by Sunday, 'the prophetic light gradually illuminating the long night'), with the widespread custom of three violet candles and one rose; violet for Advent (GIRM 346d) and the moderate floral decoration GIRM 305 asks for. The subject is the test draft x_advent_sunday, kept.

cards.subject: An early weekday Mass in Advent, before dawn, in a small stone parish church lit only by candles. At the far end, the priest stands at the altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, small, in a violet chasuble over a white alb, his hands extended in prayer; a young server in black cassock and white surplice kneels on the step at the side. The altar has a violet frontal, a crucifix and two lit candles, no flowers. In the foreground, half-length and seen from behind or in profile, a few faithful in winter coats and shawls kneel in the wooden pews, each holding a small lit candle: an old woman in a dark headscarf, a young father with his daughter, a nun in a grey habit. The tall windows are still deep blue with the first pale light at their base. Hushed, watchful, warm pools of candlelight in the dark. Keep everyone inside the arched window.
cards.frame: a thin violet ruled line just inside the gold border; the inner window is ROUND-ARCHED like a church window, edged in gold and violet; no halo
cards.basis: The ordinary weekday Mass of Advent in violet (GIRM 346d) with moderate decoration (GIRM 305), set before dawn after the collect of the week's Monday, which asks to be found 'watchful in prayer'. The candles in the pews recall the dawn Advent Masses kept in many places; the Mass shown is the weekday's own, not the Marian votive (Rorate) Mass, which would be white.

cards.subject: The Third Sunday of Advent. In the foreground, on a low stand beside the altar step, the evergreen Advent wreath with three candles lit — two violet and the ROSE one — and one violet candle still unlit. Behind it, in a brighter church, the priest stands at the altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, small, in a ROSE-coloured chasuble with gold orphreys over a white alb, his arms raised in prayer; two servers in cassock and surplice stand at either side of the step. The altar frontal is rose with gold; a crucifix and six tall lit candles on the gradine; a few small sprays of white flowers around the altar, not on it. Soft rose-gold morning light falls through the windows. Joyful but restrained. Keep everything inside the arched window.
cards.frame: a thin rose ruled line just inside the gold border; the inner window is ROUND-ARCHED like a church window, edged in gold and rose; no halo
cards.basis: GIRM 346f allows rose 'where it is the practice' on Gaudete Sunday (the repo's formulary gives the day's colour as violet, the obligatory one); the wreath's rose candle is lit this Sunday by custom. Flowers stay moderate, arranged around the altar (GIRM 305).

cards.subject: A church's Christmas crib at night during a Sunday of Christmas Time. At the side of the sanctuary, a wooden stable with a thatched roof on a bed of straw and moss, with painted carved statues (clearly statues, not living people): the Child in the manger on white linen with arms open, Mary kneeling in blue, Joseph standing with a staff, an ox and a donkey, two shepherds with a lamb; a gilded star hangs above the stable roof. Evergreen boughs, red poinsettias and many small candles glow around it. In front, half-length and seen from behind, a young mother in a Sunday coat kneels at the crib rail holding her small son, who points at the Child; behind the crib, the altar in white and gold with its candles lit. Warm golden light in the dark church, deep blue windows with stars. Keep everything inside the arched window.
cards.frame: a thin white ruled line just inside the gold border; the inner window is ROUND-ARCHED like a church window, edged in gold and white; no halo
cards.basis: The Christmas crib set up in churches, which the Directory on Popular Piety commends for Christmastide, shown on a Sunday of the season; white for Christmas Time (GIRM 346a). Carved statues keep the card apart from the living scene of `nativity_christ` and `holy_family`.

cards.subject: A Sunday morning in Ordinary Time outside a small white village church with a bell tower, its bell swinging. Families in their Sunday clothes walk up the path to the open wooden doors: a grandfather with a cane, a young couple with a baby, two children running ahead, a woman carrying a missal; they are small, half-length or seen from behind. Through the open doors, small and deep inside, the altar with lit candles and a priest in a GREEN chasuble. Around the church, green meadows, a few trees and low hills under a clear blue sky with white clouds; bright, peaceful, ordinary daylight. No lettering. Keep the church and everyone inside the arched window.
cards.frame: a thin green ruled line just inside the gold border; the inner window is ROUND-ARCHED like a church window, edged in gold and green; no halo
cards.basis: Green is the colour of Ordinary Time (GIRM 346c); the card shows the Sunday itself, the parish gathering for Mass, rather than a moment of the rite, which the parts-of-the-Mass cards paint. The Second Sunday is chosen as the formulary: the First Sunday of the season gives way to the Baptism of the Lord.

cards.subject: A Sunday Mass in Lent in a large stone parish church, stripped and sober. The altar is BARE OF FLOWERS, with a violet frontal, a large crucifix and six tall lit candles. The priest stands at the altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, small, in a VIOLET chasuble over a white alb, his hands joined, with a deacon in a violet dalmatic and two servers at his sides on the steps. In the foreground, half-length and seen from behind, a full congregation kneels in the pews, heads bowed: men, women, children, an old couple. Along the side walls, the small carved Stations of the Cross. Grey-violet morning light through tall windows. Solemn, penitent, still. Keep everyone inside the arched window.
cards.frame: a thin violet ruled line just inside the gold border; the inner window is ROUND-ARCHED like a church window, edged in gold and violet; no halo
cards.basis: Lent in violet (GIRM 346d), with the altar that GIRM 305 forbids to be decorated with flowers in this season; the collect of the First Sunday gives the season's theme, and its Gospel every year is the temptation in the desert, hence the caption.

cards.subject: A weekday Mass in Lent in a quiet side chapel on a grey early morning. The priest stands at the altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, small, in a plain VIOLET chasuble over a white alb, bowing slightly as he prays; one server kneels at the step. The small altar has a violet antependium, a wooden crucifix and two lit candles, and NO FLOWERS. On the whitewashed wall, a carved wooden Station of the Cross (Jesus falls) without lettering. A few faithful kneel half-length in the foreground, seen from behind or in profile: a man in a worn work jacket with his head bowed, an elderly woman with a black lace veil and a rosary, a young woman with joined hands. Cold, soft light from a single high window; bare and sober, but peaceful. Keep everyone inside the arched window.
cards.frame: a thin violet ruled line just inside the gold border; the inner window is ROUND-ARCHED like a church window, edged in gold and violet; no halo
cards.basis: The weekday Mass of Lent in violet (GIRM 346d) with the flowerless altar of GIRM 305; the Stations of the Cross, a devotion the Directory on Popular Piety ties to Lent, are painted as part of the chapel's walls, not as a service.

cards.subject: The Fourth Sunday of Lent: a stone parish church in which, for this one Sunday, the Lenten sobriety lifts a little. The priest stands at the altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, small, in a ROSE-coloured chasuble with gold orphreys over a white alb, his arms raised in prayer; two servers kneel at the steps. The altar frontal is rose with gold; a crucifix and six tall lit candles; for the first time in Lent, two vases of pale spring blossom (almond and white lilies) stand beside the altar, not on it. In the organ loft at the side, small, an organist at the pipes. In the foreground, half-length and seen from behind, a congregation in the pews, a child looking up at the flowers. Clear spring light, pale rose and gold, through tall windows. Keep everything inside the arched window.
cards.frame: a thin rose ruled line just inside the gold border; the inner window is ROUND-ARCHED like a church window, edged in gold and rose; no halo
cards.basis: GIRM 346f allows rose on Laetare Sunday where it is the practice (the repo's formulary gives violet, the obligatory colour); GIRM 305 and 313 make Laetare the Lenten exception for flowers at the altar and for the organ played alone, which the card paints.
